Adaptive collection workspace + 'Photos waiting' cue + sentence-case copy sweep (#253)

* UX collections flow rethink

* docs: fold second adversarial review (HIGH/MED/LOW) into adaptive-workspace spec+plan

Second 6-persona adversarial review of the adaptive collection workspace
spec+plan (Security CLEAN, rest CONCERNS, converging on an ordering defect).
Folds applied:

- Order key: both previews order with a unique tiebreaker (pool
  created_at ASC, id ASC; items number ASC); never updated_at; DB tests
  seed distinct timestamps so a LIMIT over ties is deterministic.
- Pool URL: getPoolPhotoAssetUrl (the item builder throws for pool photos).
- Owner check: isOwner = collection.ownerId === session.user.id (not the
  API-only capability machinery); previews queried by resolved collection.id.
- Items-first: one dominant action; Add item/View all items demoted.
- Access invariant: inaccessible-collection test asserts the preview repo
  was not called.
- Reuse over rebuild: bound via limit/orderBy params on existing
  findPoolByCollection/findByCollection; reuse findCoverPhotosByItemIds.
- Empty vs error: failed preview queries propagate; only per-img degrade.
- Migration: no index expected; if added, transactional migrator forecloses
  CONCURRENTLY -> note the deploy lock.
- Simplicity: only PhotoPoolPreview/ItemPreviewGrid are components; inline
  secondary/owner links; drop standalone copy-cleanup task; fold item-preview
  task into the bounded-reads task; contrast rows only for new pairings.
- Labels asserted once by role+name; quoted [id] test paths; CI DB-test
  mechanism described accurately.

* feat(repos): query-bounded pool + item preview reads

Add optional bounds to the existing collection reads for the adaptive
workspace previews — SQL LIMIT at the query layer, not a UI slice — without
new near-duplicate methods.

  bounded slice ordered by number ASC (index-backed, unique). No options means

- Reuses findCoverPhotosByItemIds (no new cover method).

bounded LIMIT 6 read uses photos_collection_id_idx for selective collections,
and a bounded top-N heapsort (about half the cost) in the worst case — strictly
cheaper than today's accepted unbounded pool read. Documented in a comment.

DB-backed tests (RUN_DB_TESTS=1): limit incl. exact-6 boundary, deterministic
created_at ASC / id ASC order under distinct timestamps + a tie, deleted /
assigned / foreign exclusions, and the pool URL via getPoolPhotoAssetUrl.
